notes: Libretto by Luigi Illica and Giuseppe Giacosa (1896). Words follow the Ricordi vocal score's spelling and punctuation (poësie with its diaeresis; Chè, stà, vo'; toast, the English word, printed in italics; Musetta's asides opened and closed with brackets as printed; the print's runs of dots after ricamata, desiata, asconde, Rodolfo?, Musetta;, Camerier!, pare! and the rest). The chorus (shopwomen, girls and students) sings in the score and is heard with the piano; only the soloists' lines are given here. IPA follows sung Italian conventions: stressed syllable marked, words sung on one note joined with ‿, open e/o as ɛ/ɔ, intervocalic s voiced. Translation literal, for meaning.
